# Case Study

Business Analytics HT26 - Umeå University

"How do changes in the US unemployment rate influence the household savings rate, and what do the relationships imply for the resilience of household spending?"

Group 17:

- Enrico Franco Conde

- Mischa Leon Pöplow

## Introduction

For this analysis, we will use the `economics` dataset from `ggplot2` https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/economics.html and `unrate` from the US Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE

Load libraries

```{r, libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(gridExtra)
```

Download and read unemployment rate

```{r, import unemployment}
fedunrate <- read_csv("https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE")

fedunrate <- fedunrate |>
  rename(date = observation_date) |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("1967-07-01"),
         date <= as.Date("2015-04-01"))

economicsWithUnrate <- economics |>
  left_join(fedunrate, by = "date")
```

## Overview

```{r, View}
glimpse(economicsWithUnrate)
View(economicsWithUnrate)
```

```{r, summary}
summary(economicsWithUnrate$psavert)
summary(economicsWithUnrate$UNRATE)
```

## Plots for 5. Descriptive analytics

Numbers

```{r, Table}
results <- as.data.frame(do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(economicsWithUnrate[c("psavert", "UNRATE")], summary)
))
results$Variable <- rownames(results)
results <- results[c("Variable", setdiff(names(results), "Variable"))]
rownames(results) <- NULL

tableImage <- gridExtra::tableGrob(results, rows = NULL)
ggsave("5summary.png", tableImage, width = 8, height = 3, dpi = 300)
```

Visuals

```{r, boxplots}
exportBoxplot <- ggplot(economicsWithUnrate) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = "Savings rate", y = psavert), fill = "blue") +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Savings rate", y = psavert, label = after_stat(y)),
               fun = median, geom = "text", vjust = -0.7) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Savings rate", y = psavert,
                   label = after_stat(paste0("Min: ", round(y, 2)))),
               fun = min, geom = "text", vjust = 1.5) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Savings rate", y = psavert,
                   label = after_stat(paste0("Max: ", round(y, 2)))),
               fun = max, geom = "text", vjust = -0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = "Unemployment", y = UNRATE), fill = "red") +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Unemployment", y = UNRATE, label = after_stat(y)),
               fun = median, geom = "text", vjust = -0.7) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Unemployment", y = UNRATE,
                   label = after_stat(paste0("Min: ", round(y, 2)))),
               fun = min, geom = "text", vjust = 1.5) +
  stat_summary(aes(x = "Unemployment", y = UNRATE,
                   label = after_stat(paste0("Max: ", round(y, 2)))),
               fun = max, geom = "text", vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment rate and savings rate",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r, line charts}
exportLinechart <- ggplot(data = economicsWithUnrate, mapping = aes(x = date, y = "Unemployment rate and savings rate")) + 
  labs(title = "Unemployment rate and savings rate over time (monthly)", y = "unemployment rate and savings rate in %") +
  geom_path(aes(y = UNRATE, color = "Unemployment rate")) +
  geom_path(aes(y = psavert, color = "Personal saving rate")) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Unemployment rate" = "red",
              "Personal saving rate" = "blue")
  )
```

Export the plots as png

```{r, export plots}
ggsave(filename = "5boxplot.png", plot = exportBoxplot, 
  width = 4,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300)

ggsave(filename = "5linechart.png", plot = exportLinechart, 
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300)
```

## Code for 7. analysis

```{r, correlation}
economicsWithUnrate |>
  arrange(date) |>
  summarise(
    same_month = cor(UNRATE, psavert, use = "complete.obs"),
    one_month_later = cor(lag(UNRATE, 1), psavert, use = "complete.obs"),
    two_months_later = cor(lag(UNRATE, 2), psavert, use = "complete.obs")
  )
```

```{r, basic linear model}
model1 <- lm(psavert ~ UNRATE, data = economicsWithUnrate)
summary(model1)
```

```{r, linear model plot}
exportModel1 <- ggplot(economicsWithUnrate, aes(x = UNRATE, y = psavert)) +
  geom_point(color = "#2A9D8F", alpha = 0.55, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = 0,
    color = "#E76F51",
    fill = "#F4A261",
    linewidth = 1.2,
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment and Personal Savings",
    x = "Unemployment rate (%)",
    y = "Personal savings rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
exportModel1
```
